tenuicruris:study:1.title: Tenuicruris piscanexum , a new addition to Australia’s rare Cretaceous bird fossils (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2026)

facts.statement: The genus Tenuicruris contains only one species, T. piscanexum, which is known from a single isolated leg bone.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Tenuicruris piscanexum, known from a single isolated leg bone.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of a nearly complete left tibiotarsus.
facts.quote: It consists of a nearly complete left tibiotarsus.

facts.statement: The generic name Tenuicruris is derived from the Latin words for 'slender' and 'leg'.
facts.quote: The generic name, Tenuicruris, combines the Latin words tenuis, meaning slender, and cruris, meaning leg.

facts.statement: The specific name piscanexum refers to the discovery of the holotype within a fish mash marker layer at the fossil site.
facts.quote: The specific name, piscanexum, is a combination of the Latin piscis, meaning fish, and nexum, meaning binding, alluding to the discovery of the holotype within the so-called fish mash marker layer identified in Richmond fosskicking sites in.

facts.statement: The holotype tibiotarsus of T. piscanexum measures 6.54 cm in length.
facts.quote: The T. piscanexum holotype tibiotarsus is 6.54 cm long.

facts.statement: T. piscanexum is distinguished by a deep depression on the outer surface of the tibiotarsus and flared distal condyles when viewed from behind.
facts.quote: Tenuicruris appears to be distinguishable from all other enantiornitheans by two autapomorphies (unique derived features): a deep fossa (depression) on the lateral (outer) surface of the tibiotarsus proximal to the distal condyle, and distal condyles that are flared when seen from behind.

facts.statement: Fossils of Tenuicruris were found in the Toolebuc Formation approximately 12 km northwest of Richmond, Queensland, Australia.
facts.quote: The Tenuicruris fossil material was discovered in outcrops of the Toolebuc Formation about 12 km northwest of Richmond in Queensland, Australia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is permanently housed at the Kronosaurus Korner Museum under accession number KK F1451.
facts.quote: The specimen is housed in the Kronosaurus Korner Museum, where it is permanently accessioned as specimen KK F1451.

facts.statement: Tenuicruris piscanexum was described as a new genus and species in 2026 by Matt A. White and colleagues.
facts.quote: In 2026, Matt A. White and colleagues described Tenuicruris piscanexum as a new genus and species of enantiornithean based on these fossil remains, designating KK F1451 as the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Tenuicruris lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Albian age.
Tenuicruris is classified as a member of the bird group Enantiornithes.
Researchers classified Tenuicruris as an indeterminate enantiornithean that is not a member of the Pengornithidae family.
facts.quote: White et al. regarded Tenuricruris as an indeterminate, non-pengornithid enantiornithean.

facts.statement: The precise phylogenetic position of Tenuicruris within Enantiornithes remains unresolved, resulting in a large polytomy in phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: As Pengornithidae remained well-resolved at the base of Enantiornithes, White et al. regarded Tenuricruris as an indeterminate, non-pengornithid enantiornithean.

rejected.statement: Tenuicruris is an extinct genus of enantiornithean bird from the Early Cretaceous of Australia.
rejected.quote: Tenuicruris (; ) is an extinct genus of enantiornithean bird known from the Early Cretaceous (Albian age) Toolebuc Formation of Australia.
